statement: You are given a non-negative integer n. Return how many bits in its binary form are 1.
Brian Kernighan's trick does this in one step per set bit: n & (n − 1) clears the lowest 1 bit of n, so repeat it and count the steps until n becomes 0.

examples.explanation: 29 is 11101 in binary. Clearing the lowest 1 bit each time gives 28, 24, 16 and then 0, so it takes four steps: 29 has four set bits.
0 has no 1 bits, so the loop never runs and the count is 0.
